programme: PRRX1-driven TGF-β/ECM-remodeling invasion (activating TNC, VEGFA, TGFB2, TGFB3) opposed by the tumor-suppressive brakes KLF6 (repressing via CDH1, MMP9, TGFB1) and SOX17 (Wnt-antagonism plus a triple CDK-inhibitor block: CDKN1A, CDKN1C, CDKN2B), with ONECUT1 sitting upstream of melanocyte lineage identity through its target MITF, and CEBPD supplying inflammatory/SASP-type signaling (IL6, TNF, PTGS2) that can feed the same invasive programme from the tumor microenvironment side.
role_in_a: In kidney papillary cell carcinoma the only factor with disease-specific literature placement is CEBPD, identified as part of a co-deregulated transcriptional-regulator network across kidney cancer subtypes (37047552) — consistent with an inflammatory/stress-response arm feeding tumor microenvironment remodeling. PRRX1 and KLF6 both score very highly in Open Targets for this disease (0.81 and 0.96 percentile respectively), suggesting genetic/omics association with the invasion-vs-suppression axis, but no retrieved paper places their mechanism specifically in kidney papillary carcinoma.
role_in_b: In melanoma the axis has direct mechanistic anchoring: PRRX1 transcriptionally activates SPARC to drive ECM remodeling and progression (40943659); KLF6 represses melanoma cell proliferation and invasion as a tumor suppressor (37955538); SOX17 shows disease-relevant, clinically-associated expression across cancers including melanoma (37643784, 36788073); and ONECUT1 differential expression tracks melanoma tumorigenesis and metastasis in transcriptome profiling (25034661), with its network target MITF tying it to melanocyte-lineage control.
shared_axis: Both tumors could converge on the same push-pull invasion circuit — a PRRX1-type ECM/TGF-β-driven invasive programme restrained by KLF6/SOX17 tumor-suppressor brakes — with CEBPD-driven inflammatory signaling in the kidney microenvironment and ONECUT1/MITF-linked lineage control in melanoma each feeding into it from a different direction; but this is a generic invasion-vs-suppression module rather than something specific to a kidney-skin pairing, since papillary RCC and melanoma share no developmental lineage or clinical association.
reasoning: The five carrying factors form a real, nameable cancer-biology circuit (EMT/ECM invasion driver opposed by two tumor-suppressor brakes, plus a lineage and an inflammatory arm), and four of them have literature placing them in melanoma specifically. But only CEBPD is placed in kidney papillary carcinoma, no source connects the two diseases through this programme, and seven of the twelve concordant factors (KCNIP3, PRDM1, TTF1, ZNF143, KLF5, TAF1, ZNF91) have no disease-specific evidence at all. Critically, the 126 patient-group comparisons come from a single independent cohort pair, so the high concordance counts reflect internal consistency within one dataset rather than replication across cohorts, which caps how much weight the counts alone can carry.
support: 40943659 — PRRX1 transcriptionally activates SPARC, driving melanoma progression/ECM remodeling; 37955538 — KLF6 represses proliferation and invasion in cutaneous malignant melanoma; 37643784 — SOX17 shows cancer-dependent expression and clinical outcome associations including in melanoma; 36788073 — SOX17 expression documented in malignant melanoma tissue alongside its use as an ovarian/endometrial marker; 25034661 — ONECUT1 differential expression detected across melanoma cell lines in tumorigenesis/metastasis RNA-seq; 37047552 — CEBPD identified among co-deregulated transcriptional regulators in kidney cancer gene regulatory networks.
how_to_falsify: In papillary RCC tumor lines/organoids, test whether PRRX1 and KLF6 co-regulate the same targets seen in melanoma (TNC, VEGFA, TGFB2/3 for PRRX1; CDH1, MMP9, TGFB1 for KLF6) via ChIP/CUT&RUN and knockdown-rescue invasion assays; if PRRX1 knockdown fails to reduce ECM/invasion markers in RCC lines, or KLF6 overexpression fails to suppress invasion there, the cross-disease axis does not hold despite the shared factor list. Separately, test whether CEBPD knockdown in RCC organoids reduces IL6/TNF/PTGS2 without any change in PRRX1-target expression — if the inflammatory arm is uncoupled from the EMT arm, the proposed convergence is wrong.
caveats: Kidney and skin epithelia share no developmental lineage, so any connection is structural, not anatomical. The 126 patient-group comparisons derive from only 1 independent cohort pair — treat high concordance (e.g., PRRX1 at 87/126) as consistency within one dataset, not cross-cohort replication. Single-view exclusions removed SOX9 (a PRRX1 target) and EZH2 among others — the account should not lean on those despite their thematic fit. No tissue-generic exclusion list was supplied for this pair. Seven of the twelve concordant factors (KCNIP3, PRDM1, TTF1, ZNF143, KLF5, TAF1, ZNF91) carry no disease-specific evidence in either disease and are excluded from the mechanistic account entirely.
